the_deleted_log_finding.what_i_found: `zones.json._deleted` is an unread experiment log. On 2026-05-27 Paul SEEDED 7 zones (`by: 'paul'`, `action: 'seeded'`): Front lawn, Pond area, Western patio, Eastern patio, Fairway meadow, Western fairway edge. `tools/draw-zones.py` shows what they were — axis-aligned RECTANGLES on guessed fractional coords, with the docstring 'Polygons are guesses — Paul corrects from there.' Between 19:25 and 20:24 that same day, a device CONFIRMED several of them repeatedly (Fairway meadow logs 15 separate `confirmed` events in 50 minutes — that's a person tapping a button over and over, i.e. testing, not ratifying), and then DELETED every single seeded zone. The next morning (02:55–03:00 UTC) the current 8 were drawn fresh in one five-minute sitting.
the_deleted_log_finding.why_it_matters: The propose-then-correct loop has already run once, end to end, and the correction was TOTAL — every proposed zone was destroyed, not adjusted. I cannot tell you who did it (`createdBy: 'device'`; the brief reads it as Paul, and that's the likely read). So this is NOT evidence about Mom. But it IS evidence about the instrument: propose-and-correct on this surface produced 'delete all eight and start over,' which is the correction a person makes when the proposal isn't close. Paul is now about to seed a second time, on the same surface, and this time the correction has to come from someone who cannot redraw polygons and cannot type. Worth knowing his first seeding pass was thrown away whole.
the_deleted_log_finding.the_15_confirms_are_the_real_warning: 'Fairway meadow' was confirmed 15 times, 'Test 2' 4 times, 'Test' once — then all deleted. The `confirm` action is idempotent, cheap, and leaves an identical trace whether it means 'yes, correct' or 'I'm poking this button.' The zone panel's `confirm` writes history but records nothing about deliberation. If Mom taps 'Looks right' on eight zones, the log will look exactly like the log from 5/27 — which we know meant nothing. Instrument this before you run it (F4).

findings.observation:
THE BASEMAP DISQUALIFIES THE WHOLE RATIFICATION. I read `images/property-map/gep-2015-03-leafoff.png` (the canonical base, `zones.json._meta.baseImage`). It is:
(a) an OBLIQUE 3-D perspective view, not an orthographic top-down — the HUD reads `eye alt 3229 ft` over `elev 2840 ft`, and the terrain is visibly tilted and foreshortened. It is not a map. It is a photograph of a hillside from an angle.
(b) MARCH 2015 LEAF-OFF (HUD: 'Imagery Date: 3/6/2015'). Eleven years stale, and every deciduous tree is a bare grey stick. The frame is ~85% undifferentiated brown.
(c) A RAW SCREENSHOT OF PAUL'S DESKTOP, with the chrome baked in: a macOS notification banner in the top-right reading 'Spotlight Importer Extension Added — Google Earth Pro added 1 Spotlight importer extension. You can manage extensions in Login Items & Extensions.'; a Google Earth Pro pin captioned 'Fernwood'; the black Google Earth HUD bar across the bottom with lat/long/elevation; the 'Google Earth' watermark.
Only four things in the entire image are legible as objects: the house roof, the driveway, the tan meadow, and a rough treeline.
findings.user_impact:
She is being asked to ratify boundaries around things the image does not show. The Western Garden and Eastern Garden are, in this photograph, brown twigs. There is no garden visible. There is no pond visible. Asking 'is the Eastern Garden drawn right?' over this image is asking her to confirm a polygon against a texture.

AND THE DATA ALREADY PROVES THIS IS WHAT HAPPENS. Of 8 zones, exactly 2 are `status: confirmed` — `fairway` and `pond-area-3`. The fairway IS the one unmistakable feature in the frame (the big tan meadow). The other 6 — Western Garden, Eastern Garden, Fairway Fringe, Lower 40, Stable Grounds, Parking Bank — are all `draft`, and all of them sit in the brown murk. The confirmed/draft split correlates exactly with what the basemap renders visible. Whoever drew these could only confirm what they could see. That is the strongest signal in this file, and it was sitting in `zones.json` the whole time.

Then there's the desktop notification. The app's canonical picture of her land has a macOS system alert about Spotlight importers pasted across the sky. For the user whose entire complaint is 'this record isn't about my place,' we are about to hand her an aerial of somebody's computer.
findings.principle_invoked: Norman — mapping and conceptual model (a map's whole job is to let the user map representation → reality; an oblique, leaf-off, 11-year-old frame breaks the mapping at the root). 'A test the user's constraints disqualify her from passing is not a test' (round 1) — she cannot see it, so her Yes means nothing and her silence means nothing. 'Trust is the load-bearing emotion' (CLAUDE.md). Nielsen #2 (match between system and the real world).
findings.recommendation:
REPLACE THE BASEMAP FIRST. Nothing in Paul's plan is worth doing over this image, and the fix is an afternoon, not a project.

Requirements, in priority order:
1. TOP-DOWN (orthographic/nadir), not oblique. This is non-negotiable and it is not a nicety — an oblique frame has no consistent scale, so a polygon drawn on it is un-reprojectable and un-georeferenceable forever. Sources: Google Maps satellite (nadir), or the county/NAIP orthoimagery (Georgia has free NAIP at ~0.6m, leaf-on, and it's public domain).
2. LEAF-ON. The gardens are the point. In March they do not exist.
3. NO CHROME. No notification banner, no HUD, no pin, no watermark. Crop it out or capture clean.
4. RECENT. 2015 predates work that has been done.
5. Keep the fractional-coord system — it's fine, and it's the reason a swap is cheap.

COST OF THE SWAP: every existing polygon breaks, because fractional coords on an oblique frame do not transfer to a nadir frame. That sounds bad and is actually free — Paul is about to redraw all 8 anyway, and 6 of 8 are `draft` (i.e. admitted guesses). This is the cheapest this swap will ever be. Do it before he adjusts, not after, or he'll do the work twice.

SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE: Paul's 'first step is I finalize the zones' has a step zero. Fix the picture, then adjust the zones on the picture, then show her.

findings.observation:
MAIN-SCREEN TAKEOVER — my position: YES to promoting the map to the front door, NO to a wizard. These are not the same move and Paul's framing bundles them.

A 'takeover' in the sense of an ordered, front-loaded, N-step interview that owns the main screen is a doctrine violation AND a bad instrument: it's a completable form with a denominator, it punishes her for stopping partway, it makes her a respondent in her own app, and it turns the front door into a task. That is the task-manager register the project is founded against, and it's also just brittle — the moment she closes it at step 3, the app has to decide whether to nag her, which is a decision Fernwood should never have to make.

But 'the map is the front door for a while' is not a wizard. It is a different card being on top.
findings.user_impact:
The doctrine says the front door is a calm glance, not a wizard — and a map of her own land seen from above IS a calm glance. It is arguably the MOST field-journal object in the entire application: it's a picture of the place, it has no state, it makes no demands, it can't be completed, and looking at it is the whole point. `zones.json._meta` already says this out loud: 'The browse view is itself a thinking tool — looking at the whole property from above helps Mom form mental models of where things are.' That sentence is the design. Somebody already knew.

So the honest move: for a bounded window, the Property Map opens at the top of the stack, expanded, with the zones drawn on it. No step counter. No 'Let's get started.' No modal. No skip button (nothing to skip). She scrolls past it if she doesn't care, exactly as she scrolls past everything else — and THAT is the instrument: if she never once touches it, that's a real finding, because a picture of her own property that she won't look at is a genuinely interpretable null.

This app does have one job right now, and Paul is right that it's honest to say so. But the honest way to say 'this is the one job' is to put the thing at the top — not to build a machine that walks her through it.
findings.principle_invoked: Field journal, not task manager (CLAUDE.md); 'For a user whose only validated behavior is opens-and-glances, an affordance must live where she already looks' (fernwood candidate); Strip teases, card holds (fernwood); the glance and the repository
findings.recommendation:
TIME-BOXED PROMOTION, NOT A WIZARD.

1. Property Map card moves to position 1 (above the composer and Mama's Perspective), expanded by default, for a defined window — call it four weeks, and put the end date in `BACKLOG.md` so it's a decision and not a drift.
2. It carries ONE line of Crimson prose above it, in the house voice, naming why it's there — the closest this app gets to an ask. Something in the register of 'Paul drew these from memory. You're the one who knows.' Content-steward writes the actual line; that's their seat, not mine. The line does the work a wizard would have done, and costs nothing when ignored.
3. NO step counter, NO progress, NO 'N of 8', NO 'get started', NO modal, NO completion state, NO nag on return. If she does nothing, the map is just a map.
4. When the window ends, the card demotes back into the stack and keeps its full function forever. Nothing is lost, nothing is 'closed.'

EXPLICITLY REJECTED: any main-screen state that (a) counts steps, (b) can be finished, (c) blocks or precedes the rest of the app, or (d) returns her to where she left off. (d) is the subtle one — 'resume where you left off' is the single most task-manager thing a surface can do, and it's the natural next idea after a takeover ships. Don't.

findings.observation:
THE ZONE-CONFIRM INTERACTION IS ALREADY BUILT — DON'T DESIGN A NEW ONE, AND ABOVE ALL DON'T BUILD A CARD QUEUE FOR IT. In `viewer.html`, `renderPropertyMap()` (7683) + `wirePropertyMap()` (7744) + the zone panel (8095–8110) already ship exactly the instrument this brief is asking for:

• Tap a zone polygon → a bottom sheet opens with the zone name at 26px in `body.text-lg`, and FOUR word-led, emoji-led, 56px-min-height buttons:
  ✓ 'Looks right' (confirm)
  ✎ 'Different name' (rename)
  🚩 'Not quite right' (flag)
  🗑 'Delete this place' (danger-styled)
• 'Different name' opens a rename submode with a text input AND A MIC (`.pmap-panel-rename-mic`, with a `.recording` state and an error hint) — she can SAY the name.
• '+ Add a place' → a popover with two paths: 📍 'Tap on the map' and 🎤 'Describe it'.
• Pan, pinch-zoom (iOS `gesture*` events), +/− buttons, reset.
• Every control has a `body.text-lg` rule. Someone built this for her specifically.
findings.user_impact:
This answers the brief's actual question — 'what affordance lets her say no, that one's wrong, or you're missing one, without writing prose?' — and the answer is: the one you already shipped, eleven months ago, and forgot about.

• 'that one's wrong' → 🚩 Not quite right, or 🗑 Delete this place.
• 'that's not what we call it' → ✎ Different name → 🎤 speak it.
• 'you're missing one' → + Add a place → 📍 tap it on the map, or 🎤 describe it out loud.

Zero prose required for any of the four disagreements. It is genuinely well-designed for her: word-led buttons (not icon-only), one tap each, big targets, mic everywhere, and the destructive action visually distinct. This is the best-fitted surface in the entire app for this user and it has never been pointed at her.

AND IT ANSWERS 'one card or eight?' — NEITHER. Eight confirm-cards is a queue with a denominator: a to-do list, a completion state, an interview that ends. One card can't hold eight zones. The MAP is the right container precisely because it is ONE OBJECT with eight taps on it and no order. There is no first zone. There is no last zone. There is no 'next.' She touches the part of her property she has an opinion about, which is the only part she'll have an opinion about anyway. A queue would force us to serve her 'Parking Bank' when she wants to talk about the Eastern Garden.
findings.principle_invoked: Recognition over recall (Nielsen #6); 'Scope is communicated by where you tap, not auto-detected' (cross-project) — tapping the polygon IS the scope declaration, which is why no zone-picker/dropdown is needed anywhere; Prefer the platform's native control; Convert origination asks into recognition asks; 'Design the end-state she described, not the tool your schema implies' (round 1)
findings.recommendation:
SHIP WHAT EXISTS. The build list for the zone step is: fix the basemap (F1), have Paul adjust the polygons, promote the card (F2), verify the panel still works on her phone, and add the acquiescence instrumentation (F4). That's it. No new surface.

Four small fixes to the existing panel, in priority order:
1. [F1 dependency] The zone LABELS render at `font-size=36` in a 1600×1103 viewBox — that's ~2.2% of frame height, which on a phone in a card is roughly 8–10 CSS px. For the no-glasses reader, on a brown photograph, that is invisible. Scale labels with viewport, not with the image, and give them a solid in-palette plate behind them (currently they're bare `<text>` over photographic noise, which is the worst possible legibility case).
2. 'Not quite right' 🚩 currently flags the zone but has no way to say WHAT is wrong without prose. Route it straight into the mic — flag → 'What's off about it?' → 🎤. Her voice, verbatim, to Paul. One extra tap, zero writing.
3. The 🚩 flag glyph is an ops-register import and violates the fernwood 'Glyphs follow the journal voice' rule (it's a JIRA/status-page idiom). It's also semantically wrong — she's not raising an incident, she's saying 'that's not it.' Replace with an in-palette mark; content-steward owns the label.
4. Verify pan/pinch still work under the card's flex context and on her actual phone. This code has not been exercised since May and the 2026-07-14 composer-order bug is the precedent for 'it worked when it shipped.'

findings.observation:
ACQUIESCENCE IS THE FAILURE MODE, AND IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The brief flags it correctly: her two 7/13 confirms were both Yes, on gimmes. Now add the `_deleted` log: 'Fairway meadow' logs FIFTEEN `confirmed` events in 50 minutes before being deleted. The `confirm` action is cheap, idempotent, and leaves a trace identical whether it means 'yes, that's right' or 'I am poking this to see what it does' or 'I want this sheet to go away.'

So we are about to run a ratification whose instrument cannot distinguish assent from dismissal — on a user who has never once said no to us, about a map she may not be able to see (F1), where 'Looks right' is the largest, first, and easiest button in the sheet.
findings.user_impact: If she taps 'Looks right' on eight zones, Paul will conclude his model of her mental map was correct. That conclusion would be worth less than nothing — it would launder his own guesses into 'confirmed by Mom' and then the plant-to-zone assignments would be built on top of it, and the record would be MORE confidently wrong than it is today, with her name on it. That is strictly worse than the current honest `status: draft`. The whole premise of Paul's reframe is 'it's not trustworthy if I do it' — an unfalsifiable Yes gives him exactly the false trust he's trying to avoid, while feeling like the opposite.
findings.principle_invoked: 'A test the user's constraints disqualify her from passing is not a test' (round 1 — direct application); Nielsen #1 (visibility of system status — applied to PAUL as the reader of the result); 'AI/agent proposals are not user-validated' (feedback_agent_proposals_not_validated); 'A value's provenance and freshness must be shown as honestly as the value itself' — a confirm has provenance too
findings.recommendation:
MAKE DISAGREEMENT AS CHEAP AS AGREEMENT, AND MAKE ASSENT FALSIFIABLE.

1. DEMOTE 'Looks right.' Right now it is first, top, and identical in weight to the others. Four co-equal buttons where the agreeable one is first and largest is a leading question rendered in CSS. Options are not neutral just because they're all present. Put 'Looks right' LAST, or make the three correction paths the visually primary group.
2. INSTRUMENT DELIBERATION, and treat a cheap Yes as null data. The rig already exists (`firstOfferedAt`, MetricsCollector). Record per confirm: time-since-panel-open, whether she zoomed/panned the map at all before answering, and whether she opened the zone more than once. A confirm that arrives <3s after the sheet opens, with no zoom, on a zone she never looked at twice, is NOT evidence. Paul must be able to see that distinction in the readout, or he will read eight Yesses as eight facts.
3. STOP WRITING BARE `confirmed` TO HISTORY. Today `action: 'confirmed'` records nothing about the act (that's how 15 identical entries happened). Carry the deliberation metadata into the history entry so the record itself is honest about how much a Yes was worth. This is the same provenance-honesty rule the variety chip already honors on the read path — apply it to the write path.
4. DEBOUNCE. Fifteen confirms on one zone should be impossible. Idempotent-and-silent, or the log lies.
5. THE HONEST FRAMING: Paul should not ask 'are these right?' He should ask, in the house voice, 'which of these is wrong?' — a question whose easy answer is not Yes. This is a one-line copy decision with more leverage than anything else in this file. Content-steward's seat.
6. THE KILL CONDITION, set in advance: if she confirms ≥6 of 8 zones in under two minutes with no zoom and no corrections, treat the ratification as FAILED, not passed. That pattern means the instrument didn't work — most likely F1. Write this down before running it, or it will be rationalized after.

findings.observation:
STEP 3 — 'name the key plants she remembers in this zone, in her own words (verbatim)' — AS SPECIFIED, THIS IS THE STEP THAT BREAKS THE PLAN. As free text on a phone it is: unaided recall (the hardest retrieval task in the catalogue), of proper nouns, spelled, typed, by a woman who WRITES with difficulty, with no anchor in view. Round 1's four disqualifiers for the table all apply here, plus a fifth that's worse: a table at least shows you the answers. This shows her a blank box and asks her to produce them from memory. It is the single hardest thing anyone has ever asked her to do in this app, and she has never completed a task one-tenth this hard.

As free TEXT: dead. Don't build it.

But the step is not dead — the INPUT MODE is what's killing it, and the fix is already in the file.
findings.user_impact:
SHE READS AND WRITES WITH DIFFICULTY. NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS SHE SPEAKS WITH DIFFICULTY. She is a conversational Claude power user — her one self-built habit, the thing she calls the difference-maker, is talking to Claude with a photo. Speech has no spelling. Speech has no fine print. Speech is the one high-bandwidth output channel she has that this app has never once asked her to use for content.

And the mic is ALREADY THERE, three times over: `.pmap-panel-rename-mic` in the zone panel, `#ui-mic-btn` on the composer (`UnifiedVoice`, restored 2026-05-21), and 🎤 'Describe it' in the add-a-place popover. The `createVoiceCapture` factory is live. This is not a build; it's a wiring job.

AND — THIS IS THE PART THAT DECIDES IT — Paul's epistemics claim REQUIRES an open channel. His whole argument is 'only she has the map, so only she can draw it.' A closed instrument (chips of our 26 plants, a picker, a checklist) can only ever CONFIRM the record we already have. It structurally cannot surface the plant we don't know about, the name the family actually uses, or the 'that one died three years ago.' A picker would answer the question 'is our record right?' — which is the round-1 question Paul explicitly moved past. Only an open channel can answer 'what's actually here?' Voice is the only open channel she has. So the epistemics argument doesn't just permit voice — it forbids everything else.
findings.principle_invoked: Recognition over recall (Nielsen #6) — and the recognition here is the MAP, not a list; 'Scope is communicated by where you tap' (cross-project) — the zone tap declares the scope, so she never has to say which zone she's talking about; 'No AI on the capture path' (feedback_no_ai_on_capture) — her recording/transcript is the record, verbatim, unclassified; Prefer the platform's native control
findings.recommendation:
REPLACE THE TEXT BOX WITH THE MIC, AND LET THE MAP BE THE PROMPT. The whole of step 3 becomes ONE button in the zone panel she's already tapping:

  🎤 'What's growing here?'

She taps her zone → the sheet is already open (F3) → she talks → verbatim to Paul. That's the elicitation. It is one tap deeper than the confirm she's already doing, in the sheet she's already in, about the patch of ground she just pointed at.

Why this works where the text box dies:
• The MAP is the recall aid. She's not staring at a blank box trying to remember what's in the Eastern Garden — she is LOOKING at the Eastern Garden. That's cued recall, not free recall, and the difference is enormous. (This is also the second reason F1 is critical: over the leaf-off image she's looking at brown sticks, and the cue does nothing. The basemap is load-bearing for step 3 too.)
• Scope is free. She tapped the zone. She never says 'in the Eastern Garden' — the polygon said it.
• 'Key plants she remembers' is HER filter, unprompted. That's the whole prize. She'll name the four that matter to her and skip the twenty-two that don't, and the four she names are worth more than all 26 rows of plants.json, because they're the ones with meaning attached.
• Verbatim is native. It IS her words — no transcription of intent, no paraphrase, no Paul-as-scribe. Paul's stated bar ('in her own words') is met by construction.

BUILD NOTES:
• Store the AUDIO, not just the SpeechRecognition transcript. Web Speech will mangle 'crocosmia' and 'Sarracenia' and every family nickname — and the nicknames are exactly the data we're mining for. If the transcript is the only record, the AI-free capture path silently becomes a lossy AI transcription of her most valuable sentence. Keep the audio as the record and let the transcript be a convenience for Paul; the `audio_ref` server-blob pattern from the tabled Phase H already exists for this.
• NO transcript shown back to her for correction. She can't proofread it and the mangling would read as the app getting her wrong.
• Ack must be honest and must be verified, per round 1 F1. On an unpaired device this whole path is a shredder with a receipt.
• AI boundary: none of this touches AI on the way in. Paul listens. Paul folds. Unchanged.

FALLBACK IF VOICE FAILS ON HER DEVICE: not a text box. The photo path she already uses — 'show me' beats 'tell me' for her, on her own proven behavior. But voice first.

HONEST CAVEAT: 'she speaks fluently' is my assumption (see user_context). It is near-certain but nobody has verified it. If it's wrong, step 3 has no solution and the plan really does break there — say so rather than shipping a text box as consolation.

findings.observation:
'ASK HER HOW SHE WANTS TO SUPPLY PICTURES' — yes, this is the anti-pattern, and it's the specific one where the answer is already sitting in the data.

Users don't know what's possible, so the question either returns 'I don't know' (most likely, and it costs her the sense that we know what we're doing) or it returns the thing she already does — in which case we've spent a question to learn something the telemetry already told us. It's also, in her specific case, a question about implementation posed to someone whose whole complaint is that the record isn't right. It moves her from 'owner of the place' to 'consultant on our roadmap.' Wrong seat.
findings.user_impact:
WE ALREADY KNOW THE ANSWER AND IT IS THE MOST VALIDATED FACT IN THE ENTIRE FILE. She has a self-built photo habit — photo-to-Claude for ID — that she invented herself, uses daily, and named as the difference-maker. TWO of the 26 plants carry real property photos and both are `source: 'Phase F submission'` — from HER workflow. Not from a feature we designed. From the thing she already does.

Asking her how she'd like to supply pictures is asking a woman who has already answered, twice, in the record, with photographs.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Defer affordances pending signal' (feedback_defer_affordances_pending_signal) — the signal exists, don't survey for it; Prefer the platform's native control; 'Design the end-state she described, not the tool your schema implies' (round 1); Nielsen #6 — asking her to imagine an affordance is recall; showing her one is recognition
findings.recommendation:
DON'T ASK. SHIP THE PATH SHE'S ALREADY ON, AND WATCH.

1. The zone panel gets a second voice-adjacent button beside 'What's growing here?': 📷 'Show me' → the NATIVE iOS camera/library sheet via a plain `<input type="file" accept="image/*">`. That element already exists at `#ui-image-file` (4824) and already feeds the Phase F commit path SHE HAS ALREADY USED TWICE. Zero new machinery. The photo lands tagged to the zone she tapped — scope, again, for free.
2. Instrument it. If she supplies photos through it, the question is answered by behavior, which is the only answer worth having. If she doesn't but keeps sending them to Paul via Claude/text, that's ALSO an answer — and the right response then is to meet her where she is (an intake for photos she sends out-of-band), not to keep building surfaces she walks past.

IF PAUL WANTS TO ASK HER SOMETHING ABOUT PHOTOS, make it PAST-TENSE and CONCRETE, not preference-shaped: 'When you sent that photo of the hydrangea — was that easy? Would you do it again?' That's a question about a real thing that really happened, which she can actually answer. 'How would you like to supply pictures?' is a design meeting, and she isn't on the design team.

findings.observation:
THE ADD/EDIT-PLANT-RECORD BUTTON — no. Not in Guru, not in the Almanac, not anywhere new.

Round 1 found three write-targets already colliding inside `#unified-input`, distinguishable only by fine print she can't read. A fourth entry point — 'add or edit a plant record: upload a picture, say whether it's new or existing, which zone, etc.' — makes the exact diagnosed problem worse, and it's ALSO the round-1 table wearing a button: 'new or existing? which zone? upload a picture' is plants.json's schema rendered as a form. It's a CRUD modal with the columns turned sideways.

And it fails the scope rule structurally: the Almanac's box is scope-blind by construction (fernwood: 'Capture needs a declared scope; a scope-blind capture control can't stay AI-free'), so a plant-record button hung off it must ask her to declare the plant AND the zone in the form — which is the picker/dropdown/typing stack she cannot use. Garden Guru is worse: it drags a canon-write control onto the ask surface, which the AI-boundary doctrine already forbids on Mom's side.
findings.user_impact: She has never once used a standing control (0/104). This would be the fourth. And it would be the fourth in the exact section she just told us was too confusing to route.
findings.principle_invoked: 'Capture needs a declared scope; a scope-blind capture control can't stay AI-free' (fernwood); 'Identical form is a promise of identical function' (round 1 proposal); 'Defer affordances pending signal'; 'Design the end-state she described, not the tool your schema implies' (round 1)
findings.recommendation:
IT ALREADY EXISTS AND IT'S THE MIC. If she taps the Eastern Garden and says 'there's a Japanese maple by the pond that you don't have' — that IS an add. If she says 'that hydrangea died two winters ago' — that IS an edit. Paul folds it, behind the same gate as every other fold. The zone panel's voice channel is the add/edit path, and it costs her nothing to learn because it's the same button she already used to say what's growing there.

WHERE IT GOES, IF ANYWHERE: for PAUL. He's the one who needs a CRUD surface over plants.json, he thinks in schemas, and he reads fine on a laptop. Round 1 F4 already said this: build the table for Paul, in `tools/`, behind the glass. It's the authoring queue that turns her recording into canon. That's where the button lives.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND: if she uses the voice channel repeatedly and starts hitting its ceiling — if Paul finds himself folding a dozen of her spoken adds a week. Then a real add-affordance has earned itself on observed behavior. Not before.

findings.observation:
THE INTERVIEW-ENDS PROBLEM (tension 2) — this dissolves rather than resolves, and it dissolves because of the object, not because of a copy trick.

A structured top-down elicitation is inherently finite: ordered, front-loaded, with a denominator. Fernwood's doctrine forbids completable forms and task-manager register. The brief asks me to square it or claim an exception. I don't need the exception. A MAP IS NOT A FORM.
findings.user_impact:
A map is a PLACE, not a sequence. It has no first item, no last item, no order, no count, and no end. It cannot be completed because there's nothing to complete — there's just the property, and some of it has names on it and some of it doesn't. She can touch one zone in July and another in October and neither one is 'resuming.' Nothing was ever pending.

This is why the map beats a card queue at BOTH questions the brief raises — it's the answer to 'one card or eight?' (F3: neither, it's one object with eight taps) AND the answer to 'but interviews end' (they do; maps don't). Those turn out to be the same question, and picking the right object answers both at once. The finite thing here was never the elicitation — it was the CARD QUEUE we were about to build to carry it.

And round 1's 'ride the season, not the backlog' — which I still hold for plants — doesn't apply to zones and doesn't need to. A zone map has no July. But it also has no deadline, no decay, and no backlog to ride. It just sits there being her land. The seasonal argument was load-bearing for plants precisely BECAUSE a plant queue is finite and would otherwise read as a chore. The map needs no such rescue.
findings.principle_invoked: Field journal, not task manager (CLAUDE.md); the glance and the repository (a map is repository-shaped: always there, never demanding, deep on tap); 'Defer affordances pending signal'
findings.recommendation:
THE DENOMINATOR MUST NOT EXIST ON HER SURFACE. Concretely, the things that would smuggle the interview back in — each of which is a natural, well-meaning next idea, which is why I'm naming them:

1. NO status rendering on her map. `status: draft | confirmed | flagged` is PAUL's data-quality field, not her progress bar. If confirmed zones render differently from draft zones, we have built a completion meter out of CSS and she will read it as 'six left.' Draw all eight the same. Paul reads status in `tools/`.
2. NO count, NO '2 of 8', NO 'zones remaining', NO checkmarks that persist, NO summary line.
3. NO ordering, NO 'next zone', NO auto-advance to the next polygon after she confirms one. Auto-advance is the wizard reincarnating inside the map.
4. NO resume state. Nothing was interrupted.
5. NO reminder, NO nag, NO 'you haven't finished.' The card demotes on the calendar (F2), silently.
6. The map is IDENTICAL on day 1 and day 40 and forever, except that it's more accurate. Nothing about it ever says 'done.'

PAUL'S SIDE gets the denominator, because Paul is the one who legitimately needs one: 6 of 8 draft, 24 of 26 unplaced, 18 of 26 stock photos. That's `tools/`. He can have all the counts he wants where she can't see them.

position_changes_from_round_1: ROUND 1 SAID: 'one card at a time, ride the season, never present N gaps at once.' I HOLD THAT FOR PLANTS and REVERSE IT FOR ZONES. Paul's epistemics argument beats my sequencing argument here, and the reason is specific rather than rhetorical: zones are not seasonal (a zone map has no July, so there's nothing to ride); there are 8 not 26; she is RATIFYING not ORIGINATING; and — decisively — the zone map is a PREREQUISITE, not a peer. Every per-plant zone question I proposed in round 1 F5B ('where does the panicle hydrangea live?' → tap a zone chip) presupposes a zone vocabulary that is TRUE. Asking her to place 24 plants into 6 draft polygons drawn from Paul's guesses over an 11-year-old oblique photo would be pouring good ground-truth into a bad container. The zones come first. Paul is right about the ordering, and round 1 had it backwards.

ROUND 1 SAID: 'never present N gaps at once — if the surface shows N, it's the table.' THE MAP SHOWS 8 AT ONCE AND IS NOT THE TABLE. I want to be precise about why, because this is exactly the kind of exception that eats a principle. A table presents N gaps as an ENUMERATION — rows, order, a denominator, an implied completion, a demand. A map presents N zones as a PLACE — no order, no count, no first, no last, nothing owed. The test in round 1 ('does the surface present N gaps at once?') was a good proxy that turns out to be measuring the wrong thing. The real test is: DOES THE SURFACE IMPLY AN OBLIGATION TO EXHAUST IT? A list does. A picture doesn't. I'd amend the round-1 rule rather than carve an exception into it.

ROUND 1 ASSUMED: 'mobile-only, one-handed, reclined, half-engaged.' NOW KNOWN INCOMPLETE — she was on a MacBook on 7/15, sitting down, typing multi-part feedback deliberately. That doesn't resurrect the table (she still reads with difficulty, and the table is still Paul's schema shipped to the user), but it does mean 'she'll never do a sustained deliberate thing' was never established. Round 1 leaned on that. It shouldn't have.

ROUND 1 SAID: 'never a standing box — the gate opened only because she asked.' I'M NOW PROMOTING A STANDING MAP TO THE FRONT DOOR. The gate is satisfied the same way: she asked for location data leveraging the zones, unprompted, in her own words. This is that ask.

what_i_would_build_in_order.note: Dependency-ordered. Steps 0–1 gate everything; do not reorder them.
steps: 0. [round 1 F1 — STILL UNFIXED, STILL OUTRANKS EVERYTHING] The write path silently no-ops on unpaired devices while showing 'Noted — it's in the record. ✓'. Her MacBook is dark. Every recording, every confirm, every photo in this plan is a shredder with a receipt until this is fixed AND her MacBook is paired. Do not run an elicitation into a void. This is the third-incident prevention and it is not a UI problem.

1. [F1] REPLACE THE BASEMAP. Top-down (not oblique), leaf-on, recent, no macOS notification banner, no Google Earth HUD, no pin, no watermark. Everything downstream is worthless without it — the ratification (F3/F4) and the recall cue for voice (F5) both depend on her recognizing her own property.
2. [Paul] Adjust/redraw the 8 zones on the NEW basemap. Do this after step 1 or the work is done twice (fractional coords do not survive an oblique→nadir swap).
3. [F1.1] Fix zone-label legibility — scale with viewport not image, solid in-palette plate behind the text.

4. [F4] Instrumentation + honesty: demote 'Looks right', record deliberation metadata (time-to-answer, zoomed?, reopened?) into the history entry, debounce repeat confirms, write the kill condition into BACKLOG.md BEFORE running.
5. [F2] Promote the Property Map card to position 1, expanded, four-week window, end date in BACKLOG.md. One line of house-voice prose above it (content-steward).
6. [F5] Add 🎤 'What's growing here?' to the zone panel. Store audio, not just the transcript. Verbatim to Paul, AI-free.
7. [F6] Add 📷 'Show me' to the zone panel — native file input, existing Phase F path, tagged to the tapped zone.
8. [F3.2] Route 🚩 'Not quite right' into the mic instead of a dead end.
9. [F3.4] Verify pan/pinch/panel on her actual device. This code hasn't run since May.
10. [round 1 F4 / F7] Paul's gap table in tools/ — the authoring queue that turns her recordings into canon.
11. [round 1 F5] ONLY AFTER the zones are true: the per-plant zone/photo cards, riding the season. Round 1's design stands; it was just sequenced too early.
explicitly_not_doing: NO wizard, NO step counter, NO N-of-8, NO 'get started', NO modal, NO resume-where-you-left-off, NO auto-advance between zones.
NO card queue for zone confirms. The map is the container.
NO free-text box for 'name the plants.' Voice or nothing.
NO chip/checklist/picker of our 26 plants for step 3 — a closed list can only confirm the record we have, which is the question Paul explicitly moved past.
NO asking her how she'd like to supply pictures. She already answered, twice, in the record.
NO add/edit-plant-record button in Guru or the Almanac. Fourth standing control, scope-blind, CRUD-shaped.
NO status rendering (draft/confirmed) on her map — that's a progress bar in disguise.
NO ratifying anything on the 2015 oblique leaf-off screenshot.
NO AI anywhere on this path. Her voice is the record, verbatim, untranscribed-for-meaning, unclassified. Paul listens; Paul folds; the gate is unchanged.

where_i_think_pauls_plan_is_wrong: STEP ZERO IS THE PICTURE, AND IT ISN'T IN THE PLAN. 'First I finalize the zones, then she confirms' has an unstated dependency: she has to be able to SEE her property. The current basemap is an oblique, 11-year-old, leaf-off Google Earth screenshot with a macOS notification about Spotlight importers baked into the sky. The evidence that this is already the binding constraint is sitting in zones.json: the only 2 zones ever confirmed are the only 2 features the image renders legibly. The other 6 are drafts in brown murk. Fix the picture first, then adjust the zones, or the adjustment gets done twice and the ratification means nothing.

'PROPOSE → SHE CONFIRMS' HAS AN ACQUIESCENCE PROBLEM YOU'VE ALREADY SEEN TWICE. Her 7/13 confirms: 2 for 2 Yes on gimmes. The `_deleted` log: 'Fairway meadow' confirmed 15 times in 50 minutes, then deleted. `confirm` is cheap, idempotent, and indistinguishable from poking. If she taps 'Looks right' eight times, your conclusion will be 'my model of her map was correct' — which is precisely the false confidence your reframe exists to avoid, laundered through her name. Make the easy answer 'which one is wrong?', demote 'Looks right', instrument deliberation, and set the kill condition in advance.

STEP 3 AS WRITTEN IS THE STEP THAT BREAKS IT — BUT ONLY BECAUSE OF THE INPUT MODE. 'Name the key plants you remember, in your own words' as free text is unaided recall of proper nouns, typed, by someone who writes with difficulty. Dead on arrival. As VOICE, with the map open and the zone tapped, it's the best idea in your plan: the map does the recall work, the tap does the scoping, and 'in her own words' becomes literally true. The mic is already built in that exact panel.

YOU'RE DESIGNING A SURFACE YOU ALREADY BUILT. renderPropertyMap + wirePropertyMap + the zone panel already ship tap-a-zone → 'Looks right / Different name (with a MIC) / Not quite right / Delete this place', plus '+ Add a place → Tap on the map | 🎤 Describe it', with pinch-zoom and body.text-lg rules on every control. That is the confirm-and-correct instrument this brief is asking me to design, and it's the best-fitted surface in the app for her. It has never been pointed at her. zones.json._meta even states the thesis: 'The browse view is itself a thinking tool.' Somebody already knew.

'HOW DO YOU WANT TO SUPPLY PICTURES' IS A DESIGN MEETING, AND SHE ISN'T ON THE DESIGN TEAM. She answered this question already, twice, in the record — the only 2 real property photos in plants.json came from her own photo-to-Claude habit, the thing she invented and calls the difference-maker. Ship the native photo sheet in the zone panel and watch. If you must ask, ask past-tense about a real photo she really sent.

THE ADD/EDIT-RECORD BUTTON IS THE TABLE WEARING A BUTTON. 'Upload a picture, say whether it's new or existing, which zone' is plants.json's schema turned sideways into a form — and it would be the fourth standing control for a user who's used zero, in the section she just told us she can't route. The mic is the add path: 'there's a Japanese maple by the pond you don't have' IS an add. The CRUD surface belongs to you, in tools/.

AND — I WAS WRONG IN ROUND 1 ABOUT THE ORDER. 'Ride the season, one card at a time' still holds for plants, but zones aren't seasonal and they're a prerequisite, not a peer. Every per-plant zone card I proposed presupposes a zone vocabulary that's true. You're right that this comes first.
open_questions_for_user: THE ONE THAT'S STILL UNANSWERED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: are the 8 zone names the family's vernacular or your inventions? 'Lower 40' / 'Stable Grounds' / 'Parking Bank' sound like they've been said out loud for years; 'Fairway Fringe' sounds authored. If they're hers, ratification is a formality and the real prize is step 3. If they're yours, the names are the FIRST thing to test — and the ✎ 'Different name' + mic path is how, because a name she has to read is a name she'll accept.

You say you have 'a pretty clear picture of how she wants the zones set up.' Where does that picture come from — has she described it, or is it your read? Not rhetorical: your whole reframe is 'it's not trustworthy if I do it.' If the adjusted set is your inference, then 'Paul adjusts → she confirms' reintroduces exactly the anchor you're trying to escape, one step earlier. That's survivable IF disagreement is genuinely cheap (F4). It's fatal if it isn't.

Your first zone seeding (5/27, 7 rectangles via draw-zones.py) was deleted wholesale within the hour and redrawn from scratch the next morning. Was that you? If someone else did it, that's the most important behavioral data in this project and I've read it wrong.

The basemap swap breaks every existing polygon (oblique → nadir doesn't transfer). I'm treating that as free because you're redrawing anyway and 6 of 8 are drafts. Confirm — if you were planning to nudge vertices rather than redraw, the order matters a lot.

Voice rests on an assumption nobody has checked: that she'll talk to her phone. She talks to Claude, so I'd bet heavily on yes — but if she won't, step 3 has no fallback I believe in (the photo path is second-best, and a text box is not an option). Worth 30 seconds of your knowledge of her before we build on it.

The four-week window on the map promotion (F2) is my number, not a derived one. Pick one you'll actually honor — the point is that it's a decision with an end date in BACKLOG.md, not that it's 28 days.
follow_up_research_suggested: engineering-partner: the basemap swap. Nadir orthoimagery source (NAIP is free/public-domain/leaf-on for Georgia at ~0.6m; Google Maps satellite is nadir), the re-drawing path, and whether to georeference properly this time so the polygons survive the NEXT swap. Also: `zones.json.propertyZones` in property.json is still the shipped placeholder — the SSOT violation the brief flagged, unresolved.
engineering-partner: round 1 F1 / F7 — the unpaired-device silent no-op. Her MacBook is a primary device and it is dark. This gates everything in this file.

content-steward: three copy decisions with outsized leverage — (1) the one line of house-voice prose above the promoted map; (2) reframing the ask from 'are these right?' to 'which of these is wrong?' (F4.5); (3) the 🎤 button label ('What's growing here?' is my placeholder) and a replacement for the ops-register 🚩 flag.
user-researcher: the zone-name provenance question (vernacular vs Paul's inventions). This is answerable by asking Paul, and it changes what the ratification is FOR.

ai-advisor: NO seat on this path — it's deterministic by construction, and I'm flagging that deliberately. The one place AI will try to creep in is transcribing her recording (see F5 build notes): if the Web Speech transcript becomes the record, the AI-free capture path has quietly become a lossy model read of her most valuable sentence, and it will mangle exactly the words we're mining for (nicknames, 'crocosmia'). Store the audio. Paul listens.

principles_to_propose.principle: A ratification instrument must make disagreement at least as cheap as agreement. Before shipping any confirm/approve/ratify surface, check what the path of least resistance is. If 'yes' is the first, largest, or only one-tap option and every correction costs more, you have built a leading question in CSS — and a Yes from it is not evidence, it's the shape of the button. Demote the agreeable option, make at least one correction path equally cheap, ask 'which of these is wrong?' rather than 'is this right?', and instrument deliberation (time-to-answer, did they even look) so a cheap Yes can be recognized as null rather than counted as a fact.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F4. Two independent occurrences already in this project: Mom's 7/13 confirms (2-for-2 Yes on gimmes, which the panel itself flagged as suspicious) and the `_deleted` log's 15 identical `confirmed` events on a zone that was then deleted. It's the acquiescence-bias problem, and it's the natural companion to the round-1 proposal 'A test the user's constraints disqualify her from passing is not a test' — that one says check whether a null result is interpretable; this one says check whether a POSITIVE result is interpretable. Generalizes anywhere Paul confirms agent-drafted work (the fold gate, the harvest gate, /verify-claim, the thesis Examiner panel — everywhere a human is asked to approve a machine's draft and 'approve' is the easy button). Candidate — but arguably 2 occurrences on day one.

principles_to_propose.principle: When a user can't write, the open channel is speech — and a closed list can only confirm the record you already have. If the goal is to learn what you don't know (their vocabulary, their model, the thing missing from your schema), a picker/checklist/chip-set structurally cannot deliver it: it can only return a subset of your own data. Reach for the open channel and pick the input mode the user actually has. Reading difficulty is not speaking difficulty; they are different faculties and conflating them costs you the entire elicitation. Corollary: store the recording, not the transcription — a speech-to-text pass on the capture path is a model read, and it mangles exactly the proper nouns and nicknames that made the utterance worth capturing.
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F5. This is the resolution of the brief's central tension (anchoring vs. her reading constraint) and it resolves rather than splits it: the anchoring horn says 'don't hand her a closed list,' the constraint horn says 'don't hand her a blank text box,' and voice-with-a-visual-cue is neither. The corollary is the important half and it's a live risk — Fernwood's AI-free capture doctrine would be quietly violated by a Web Speech transcript becoming the record. Likely generalizes: Bolo (band members who won't type), Hillyer (verbatim testimony), the phone ratification surface. Candidate — 1 occurrence.

principles_to_propose.principle: Pick the object, and the register follows. When a surface's content is inherently finite (an interview, an audit, a backlog, a set of gaps) but the product's register forbids task-manager framing, don't fight it with copy — change the object. A LIST implies an obligation to exhaust it: it has an order, a first, a last, and a denominator, and no amount of gentle wording removes them. A PLACE (a map, a picture, a room) holds the same N items with no order, no count, and nothing owed. The tell that you picked wrong: you're writing copy to make a queue feel calm, or arguing for an exception to your own tone doctrine. Amends the cruder test 'does the surface present N gaps at once?' — the real test is 'does the surface imply an obligation to exhaust it?'
principles_to_propose.rationale: From F8, and it's the reason I didn't need the exception the brief offered me. It also amends my own round-1 rule, which is why it's worth naming: round 1 said 'if the surface presents N gaps at once, it's the table' — a good proxy that measures the wrong thing. The map presents 8 at once and is the least task-manager object in the app. Same insight answers 'one card or eight?' (neither — one object with eight taps) and 'but interviews end' (they do; maps don't), which suggests the underlying rule is real rather than a rationalization. Fernwood is the origin but this is not Fernwood-specific — the Kanban board, the career scanner triage queue, and the thesis ratification surface are all list-shaped things where the object choice was never questioned. Candidate — 1 occurrence.
